rows: Arc de Triomphe, Paris

Édouard Baldus photographed the Arc de Triomphe in Paris around 1860, when the city around it was being rebuilt by Baron Haussmann. Wide new avenues were cut to spread out from the arch like the spokes of a wheel.
How many avenues do you think meet at the arch?
View from the Dominican Convent, Chalais
Félix Thiollier photographed a landscape near Grenoble in the French Alps. He brought the mood of painters from Barbizon to the camera, with misty hills and deep shadows.
What mood do the hills and shadows give you?
Young Woman in a Patterned Dress
A young woman poses in a dress with a busy pattern. The photographer thought more about the dress and the pose than about the sitter's personality, which is why it looks so formal.
Does the pattern or the woman catch your eye first?
Caryatids of the Ramesseum

The Abdullah Frères were Armenian brothers who ran a famous studio in Istanbul and Cairo. They photographed the ruins of the temple of Ramesses II at Thebes, with its tall statues standing like columns.
Why would a statue be used as a column?
Karnak, the Pylon of Horus
Henri Béchard photographed the broken gateway at Karnak in Egypt, flanked by figures of the god Horus. The empty, silent ruins seem lonely against the sky.
What would it have looked like when it was new?
Mount Edgcumbe House, Plymouth
Francis Frith photographed a large house and park on the coast of Devon, England. Frith sold prints of towns and views, and they were bought by travelers as souvenirs.
What would you do at a house by the sea?
Count Cavour
Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour, was the first prime minister of a united Italy. Charles Marville photographed him in 1860, the year Italy came together as one country.
Why might a new country want pictures of its leaders?
Nadar, Self-Portrait
Nadar was a French photographer, balloonist and cartoonist, and he photographed himself with his wild hair and bold look around 1860. He is the man who took the first aerial photos from a balloon.
What do you think it would be like to take pictures from a balloon?
Alexander Dallas Bache
Alexander Dallas Bache was a scientist who led the U.S. Coast Survey, which made maps of the American coast. Mathew Brady photographed him around 1860.
Why would a country need maps of its coast?
Abraham Lincoln, Candidate for President

Mathew Brady photographed Abraham Lincoln on the day of his Cooper Union speech in New York in February 1860. Lincoln said the picture helped to make him president, because people saw a thoughtful, strong face.
Why would a photograph help someone win an election?
John Potter Stockton
Brady photographed John Potter Stockton, a New Jersey politician, around 1860. The Library of Congress first named him wrongly as another Stockton, and the mix-up was fixed later.
Why do names get mixed up in old photographs?
Rejlander, Self-Portrait
Oscar Rejlander, a Swedish photographer who worked in England, photographed himself around 1860. He is best known for combining many negatives into one big picture.
Why would someone enjoy making pictures of themselves?
Monsieur Merlen
André Adolphe-Eugène Disdéri patented the carte-de-visite in 1854: a small photograph on card that was cheap to make and could be traded like a visiting card. Monsieur Merlen sat for one in 1861.
Why would you trade photographs of friends?
The Imperial Court of Napoleon III
Disdéri made a mosaic of cards with portraits of the people around Emperor Napoleon III. It worked like a visual catalog of important people for the public.
Who would you put on a catalog of famous people?
Railway Bridge over the Aran River
Édouard Baldus photographed the new railway from Toulouse to Bayonne in 1861. He made huge panoramas by joining several negatives.
How would you make one picture from three?
Battlefield of Gaines' Mill, Virginia
John Reekie photographed the quiet ground where a big Civil War battle had been fought in June 1862. People wanted to see the places they had read about in the newspapers.
Why would a field be a historic place?
Ruins of Richmond, Virginia
Andrew J. Russell photographed the burned center of Richmond, the Confederate capital, in April 1865. Fire had destroyed much of the town when the Confederates left.
What do you think the people did after the fire?
Ruins of the Central Church, Charleston
The Civil War left church walls like this standing in Charleston, South Carolina. The city was bombarded for a long time, and photographers recorded the broken buildings.
How can a building stand when its roof is gone?
Rue des Grands Carmes, Marseille
Adolphe Terris photographed a narrow old street in Marseille, France. Cities like this were being modernized, and his picture records the old stone streets.
What would it be like to walk down this street?
Young Girl Seated on Straw, Leaning on a Basket
Edmond Bacot photographed a young girl sitting outdoors on straw. In the 1860s, photographers and painters liked scenes of country life, and some made them in a way that looks very peaceful.
What do you think the girl is thinking?
A Mummified Cat
Charles Marville photographed a cat that had been mummified, found during excavations at Saint-Germain-en-Laye. Strange objects like this were studied by scientists and displayed in museums.
Why might someone mummify a cat?
Antietam: Bodies near the Dunker Church

Alexander Gardner arrived at Antietam, Maryland, two days after the bloodiest day of the Civil War, on September 19, 1862. When Mathew Brady's gallery showed his pictures, it was the first time many Americans saw the dead on a battlefield. This one is hard to look at, but it changed how people thought about war.
Why do you think this picture shocked people in 1862?
Cub Run, Virginia: Destroyed Bridge
George Barnard photographed a bridge destroyed in the fighting near Bull Run. Armies burned bridges to slow each other down, and photographs showed the damage.
Why would an army destroy a bridge?
Ruins of Mrs. Judith Henry's House, Bull Run
Judith Henry was an elderly widow who died in the first battle of Bull Run in 1861 when shells hit her home. Barnard photographed the ruined house, which sat in the middle of the battlefield.
Why do you think the house was in the way?
Ruins of the Stone Bridge, Bull Run
George Barnard photographed the stone bridge at Bull Run, Virginia, which was destroyed in the war. The bridge was a main crossing that both armies fought over.
Why would soldiers fight over a bridge?
Ruins of the Old Church, Hampton
Barnard photographed the ruins of an old church in Hampton, Virginia, burned in 1861 during the Civil War. It had been built in the 1600s, and the walls survived.
Why might a church wall stand after a fire?
Frieze by Cavelier: Minerva and the Muses
Adolphe Terris photographed a sculpted frieze, a long decorated band of stone, in Marseille. Photographers helped artists and architects by copying sculptures.
Can you find the goddess Minerva in the frieze?
Julia Jackson
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed her niece Julia Jackson in 1863 with a soft focus and gentle light. Julia later became the mother of the writer Virginia Woolf.
What do you notice about the soft focus?
Shimla, the Yarrows and Neighboring Hills
Samuel Bourne photographed the hills near Shimla, the hill town in northern India where British officials spent the summer. He carried a huge camera and a team of porters.
How many porters would you need to carry a camera like that?
Hyree Lake, South End
Samuel Bourne photographed a lake in the hills near Shimla, India, in 1863. His landscapes were sold in London and in India.
What does the water do to the hills' reflection?
The Manga Valley, Upper Himalayas
Bourne photographed the Manga Valley in the high Himalayas in the 1860s. Hauling his camera, glass plates and a darkroom tent through the mountains took weeks.
What would you need to carry on a trip like that?
Harkundu Village with Traveller's Bungalow
Bourne photographed a mountain village with a rest house for travelers. These stops on the new road made it possible for Europeans to travel in the Himalayas.
Why would a mountain road need a rest house?
The New Road between India and Tibet
Samuel Bourne photographed the new road cut into the mountains between India and Tibet. The alpine landscape with its sharp slopes fascinated him.
How would it feel to walk along this road?
Deodars near the China Mountains
Bourne photographed tall deodar cedar trees in the foreground of the snowy peaks. He liked to put trees in front of mountains to give scale.
How does a tree help you judge the size of a mountain?
The City of Lahore
Samuel Bourne photographed the old city of Lahore, now in Pakistan, from the roof of a house in 1863. Rooftops, domes and minarets spread to the horizon.
How many domes can you count?
Nadar in Native American Costume
Nadar, who loved to dress up, posed in a feathered headdress and costume in 1863. The photograph shows how Europeans in the 1800s often played at costumes from other cultures.
Why do you think people dressed up for portraits?
Confederate Dead, Gettysburg
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed the fields of Gettysburg in July 1863 right after the great battle. These pictures were published and made a huge impression on the public.
Why would the pictures matter to people far away?
A Sharpshooter's Position, Gettysburg

Alexander Gardner photographed a stone barricade at the foot of Little Round Top, Gettysburg, where a Confederate sharpshooter had died. The picture is famous, and it was later learned that Gardner moved the body to pose it.
Why does it matter if a photograph is staged?
Gettysburg After the Battle
Alexander Gardner photographed the Gettysburg battlefield after the fighting ended in 1863. Soldiers were gathering the dead for burial.
What do you think the men were feeling?
Unfit for Service: Artillery Caisson, Gettysburg
Alexander Gardner photographed a broken artillery cart and a horse after the fighting at Gettysburg. A caisson held ammunition for the cannon.
How did horses help an army?
St. Agnes
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed a young woman as St. Agnes in 1864. She dressed her models like saints and characters from poems, and used a soft focus that made her pictures dreamy.
How does the soft focus change the feeling?
Sojourner Truth

Sojourner Truth was born into slavery in New York and escaped with her baby daughter. She became a famous speaker for freedom and women's rights, and she sold portraits like this with the words 'I sell the shadow to support the substance.'
What do you think she meant by that?
Reverend James Langton Clark and Son
Lewis Carroll, the author of Alice in Wonderland, was also a keen photographer. He photographed a clergyman and his son in 1864.
Which character from Alice would you like to see photographed?
Cathedral Rocks and Reflections, Yosemite
Charles Leander Weed made the first photographs of Yosemite Valley in 1859. His 1864 picture of Cathedral Rocks shows the giant cliffs reflected in the still water of the Merced River.
Where does the cliff end and its reflection begin?
La Belle Jardinière Department Store
Charles Marville photographed a clothing department store in Paris during its construction. Department stores were a new invention, and they changed how people shopped.
What do you think the first department store sold?
The d'Orléans Family at Orleans House
Camille Silvy, a French photographer working in London, photographed the royal d'Orléans family in a garden party. His studio used painted backdrops and elaborate poses.
Why would a family have a big garden party?
Abraham Lincoln, 1864
Mathew Brady photographed President Abraham Lincoln in 1864. Lincoln, tired and lined by the Civil War, looks older than his age.
What does the president's face tell you about the war?
Abraham Lincoln, President of the United States
Mathew Brady's studio took portraits of Lincoln throughout the Civil War. This picture became one of many printed as small cards that people collected.
Why would people collect portraits of the president?
Sarah Bernhardt, 1864
Nadar photographed the young actress Sarah Bernhardt around 1864, before she became world famous as the Divine Sarah. She poses with a calm and clear look.
What does she look like she is about to do?
Cedars of Lebanon
Félix Bonfils photographed the ancient cedar trees of Lebanon, famous in the Bible. After he moved to Lebanon he opened a studio that sold pictures to travelers.
Why are old trees special to people?
Landscape with Ruin
Félix Thiollier photographed an old ruin standing in a quiet landscape in France. He mixed ruins and nature as painters had.
What story do you imagine for the ruin?
Stage Frieze and Cornice
Louis-Émile Durandelle photographed the decorations for the new Paris Opera house. He was one of the best architectural photographers of his day.
Why photograph decorations before they are installed?
Robert Browning
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed the poet Robert Browning in 1865. Her famous portraits of poets and scientists are soft and a little blurry on purpose.
What do you imagine a poet thinking about?
Dolmen, Cap del Puetch, Ariège
Arthur Taylor photographed an ancient stone tomb called a dolmen in southern France. The giant stones were set up thousands of years ago.
How do you think people moved such huge stones?
St. Mark's Square in Moonlight, Venice
Carlo Naya photographed an empty, moonlit Piazza San Marco in Venice in the 1860s. It may have been taken in daylight, then printed to look like night.
How could a daytime photograph look like night?
Rue Jean-de-Beauvais, Paris
Charles Marville photographed a medieval street in Paris that was to be torn down to make room for new roads. He recorded the narrow, crooked streets of old Paris before they disappeared.
Why would a city tear down old streets?
Kenilworth Castle, Warwickshire
Adolphe Braun photographed the red stone ruins of Kenilworth Castle in England. The castle had been a tourist attraction since the late 1700s, helped by Sir Walter Scott's novel Kenilworth.
What parts of the castle are still standing?
Shimla
Dr. John Murray photographed Shimla, the hill station in the Himalayan foothills where the British government retreated in summer. The town looks very different today.
Why did people go to the hills in summer?
Buktawur's Tank, Ulwur

Louis-Théophile Marie Rousselet was a French traveler who felt his drawings did not show the splendor of India's monuments, so he took up photography. This is a large stone water tank with steps in Alwar.
What do you think the steps were for?
Upper Stories of Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
Rousselet photographed the upper terraces of Akbar's tomb at Sikandra, near Agra, India. The great Mughal emperor lies buried there in a red sandstone building.
How many levels can you count?
A View in the Gardens, Sikandra
Rousselet photographed the formal gardens around Akbar's tomb in India. Mughal gardens were laid out in neat squares with water channels.
How are the gardens arranged?
Entrance of the Palace of the Padishahs, Delhi
Rousselet photographed the entrance to the Red Fort, the palace of the Mughal emperors, in Delhi. He worked for the French government on a huge project to record India.
What would it be like to enter a palace through this gate?
Wives of Jung Bahadur and His Youngest Son
Bourne and Shepherd, a studio in India, photographed relatives of Jung Bahadur Rana, the prime minister of Nepal. Photographs like this recorded the court dress of the time.
What details of the clothing do you notice?
Performers
Lai Fong ran a successful photography studio in Hong Kong. This picture of performers shows costumes and poses for an audience far away.
What kind of show do you think they performed?
Stone Horses
Lai Fong photographed a row of stone horse statues, probably along a road at a tomb in China. His pictures were sold to travelers and visitors.
Why do you think people carved horses in stone?
Rue de Constantine, Paris
Charles Marville photographed a street in Paris in the 1860s, part of his series on the city that Baron Haussmann was rebuilding. His photographs show the old city and new boulevards side by side.
What changes would a new boulevard bring?
Alfred Waud
Alfred Waud was an artist who drew scenes of the Civil War for newspapers. Mathew Brady photographed him around 1865.
Why would a newspaper still need artists?
Nadar's Revolving Self-Portrait
Nadar took a series of self-portraits turning his head, like a little movie. He liked jokes and tricks with the camera.
How many different views of his face can you see?
